summary: Jerome Silbergeld worked in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He earned a B.A. and Ph.D. at Stanford and an M.A. at the University of Oregon. He held posts at the University of Washington (~1975–2001) and Princeton University (~2001–2018).

Linguist Jerzy Bańczerowski studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956–1961). He served there as head of the Department of General and Comparative Linguistics in 1969 and as professor from 1977 to 1991.

Jerzy Kuryłowicz was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Lviv (~1920–1923) and under Antoine Meillet (~1923–1925), later holding posts at the University of Lviv (~1926–1946) and Jagiellonian University (~1946–1965).

Jessie Pons is a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed a doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University by 2011 and was attested as a junior professor at Ruhr University Bochum in 2019.
Jesung Woo works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Woo earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and held a post at Dongguk University, attested between 2001 and 2003.
Jey Flick works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Flick studied under Sheldon Pollock and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley.
Jian Ouyang was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Yang Renshan (~1904–1911). He founded the China Institute of Inner Learning and served as its head from ~1922 to 1943.

Jiang Wu specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Nankai and Harvard universities, supervised by Tu Weiming, Robert M. Gimello, and Zhichao Chen. He held a professorship at the University of Arizona (attested 2011–2018).
Jianming Hu works in Buddhist studies. Hu studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and held a researcher post at Komazawa University (attested 2015).
Jiayao An works in history, archaeology, and Sinology. She studied under Su Bai (~1979–1982) and held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and its Institute of Archaeology from ~1982.
Jien Abe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied as a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973). He served as a professor at Meiji University until 2001.

Jigdal Dagchen Sakya was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse. He held a post at the University of Washington (~1960–1963).

Jigme Chhoeda is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Druk Sangag Choeling and Tango monasteries. He served as abbot of Tango Monastery (~1986) and held posts at Dratshang Lhentshog and the Central Monastic Body.
Jigme Chökyi Sengge is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje and Dilgo Khyentse.
Jigme Pema Wangchen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dzi Gar Khenpo Nor Yang, Drukpa Khenpo Ngawang Chödrak, and Mi-pham-bśad-sgrub-chos-kyi-ñin-byed-mchog.
Jigme Tenpai Nyima studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2013) under the supervision of Yongdong Shi, and also studied under Hui Xian.
Jikai Fujiyoshi was a scholar of Buddhist studies who held a post at Kyoto University (attested 1967) and served as a professor at Rissho University.

Jikido Takasaki was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned degrees at the University of Tokyo and Pune University under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale, later serving as professor at the University of Tokyo and president of Tsurumi University.

Jim G. Shaffer is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a B.A. at Arizona State University and a Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later serving as professor of anthropology at Case Western Reserve University (~1978).
